_readme: CONTENT LEAD: drop the course PDFs in this folder, then run
.venv/Scripts/python.exe backend/scripts/ingest_pdfs.py
This file is OPTIONAL. Any PDF here that is not listed below is ingested as
a textbook titled after its filename. List a file only when you want to
override that:
title  what a student sees on a citation. Use the real book title -- it is
printed verbatim under 'Show Source', so 'hcv1' looks broken there.
kind   syllabus | textbook | notes | assignment
course a course code from backend/data/seed/course.json (default: primary)
kind='assignment' is load-bearing. Assignment material is searchable so the
graded-work guardrail can RECOGNISE homework, but it is never quoted as a
lesson source. A problem set ingested as 'textbook' would be handed to a
student as course material -- put every graded item under 'assignment'.
PDFs themselves are gitignored (too large); this manifest is committed, so a
teammate can see what the corpus is made of without the files.
Scanned PDFs with no text layer cannot be ingested -- OCR is out of scope.
Check with: ingest_pdfs.py --dry-run (it reports pages-with-text).
A reflowable source (.epub) is laid out to a fixed-page PDF at A4 / 11pt
before ingestion, because 'page 143' means nothing until a paper size and a
font size are fixed. Those page numbers are reproducible but they are OUR
rendering's, not the printed book's. Where a real PDF of the same title
exists, prefer it -- its pages match a physical copy.

files.title: Practical C Programming (Harwani, Packt 2020)
files.note: 5th-semester CSE core reading for Programming with C, 2024-25 admission batch. Source is an EPUB, so cited pages are this A4/11pt rendering's.
